documents.t: Example 2 · Follow a teammate with a throttled health label
Sparrow provides everyday administration commands, homes, warps, teleport requests, random teleportation and custom death messages for Paper and Folia.

The examples use a quest reward and a chest shop. Add your server’s Sparrow build as a compile-only dependency and declare Sparrow as a server dependency so it loads first. The variables playerId, buyer and seller are player UUIDs.
Use net.momirealms.sparrow.service.highlight.Highlight to show block outlines to local players. The service starts with Sparrow and remains available when the command is disabled.

A waypoint shows one local player a marker for a target. The viewer sees the marker, the target is the real location, and the anchor is where the marker is drawn. A distant target can have an anchor close to the viewer. Arrival checks and distance labels still use the real target.

Set economy: true in modules.yml and restart. Use /money or /coins for coins and /points for points. Each wallet starts at zero for each currency.
Configure the command switch, permission and aliases in commands.yml. Plugins can also use the Highlight API.

Sparrow provides everyday administration commands, homes, warps, teleport requests, random teleportation and custom death messages for Paper and Folia. Use Commands and permissions as a quick reference. Feature pages cover usage and essential configuration; developers can start with the Teleport API.

File Contents config.yml Database, Redis and other base settings. server.yml This server's ID and tags. commands.yml Command entry points, switches and permissions; restart after editing. modules.yml Feature module switches. features/ Separate configuration files for each module. Use /spr feature-list in game to open the module list. Select a module to check its state and hot toggle support. Its detail dialog offers a toggle when permitted. /spr feature-enable <module> and /spr feature-disable <module> change the current state without saving it. Edit modules.yml to keep your choice after a reload or restart. Run /spr reload after editing settings; its feedback identifies changes that need a restart. Cross-server features require shared database and Redis connections, plus the Sparrow companion plugin on the proxy. PlaceholderAPI is optional for text placeholders; LuckPerms provides permission lookups. Cross-server respawn needs a plugin that syncs the death state between servers, such as SparrowSync.

The examples use a quest reward and a chest shop. Add your server’s Sparrow build as a compile-only dependency and declare Sparrow as a server dependency so it loads first. The variables playerId, buyer and seller are player UUIDs.

EconomyApi api = EconomyApi.get(); if (api == null) return; EconomyCurrency coin = api.currency("coin"); if (coin == null) return; When the module is unavailable, get() returns null. Look up the currency by its file ID (coin for coin.yml). An unknown ID returns null. Pass the resulting EconomyCurrency to wallet operations, or use api.currencies() to list registered currencies.

var reward = api.give(playerId, coin, new BigDecimal("12.50"), "QuestPlugin"); var debit = api.take(playerId, coin, new BigDecimal("2.00"), "QuestPlugin", "Entry fee"); Supply an actor for every write so an administrator can identify its origin in history. The reason is optional. Construct BigDecimal from a decimal string. Wallets round to four decimal places on input and round down to the currency’s precision for display. api.transfer(buyer, seller, coin, new BigDecimal("18.75"), "ChestShop", "3 golden apples") .whenComplete((result, error) -> { if (error != null) { logger.log(java.util.logging.Level.SEVERE, "Payment failed", error); return; } if (result.status() == EconomyResult.Status.SUCCESS) { logger.info("Paid. Buyer: " + result.balance() + ", seller: " + result.recipientBalance()); } else { logger.info("Payment declined: " + result.status()); } }); Use transfer to debit the buyer and credit the seller in one transaction, including offline and cross-server accounts. Insufficient funds returns INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS normally. Other refusals include INVALID_AMOUNT, SAME_ACCOUNT and TRANSFER_DISABLED. Deliver items only after SUCCESS, scheduling inventory changes on the appropriate server thread. On one backend, writes sharing an account run in acceptance order. The database orders writes across backends. If a second operation requires the first to succeed, check its status before submitting the second with thenCompose.

Use api.peekBalance(playerId, coin) for a synchronous snapshot. It returns null until ready. For an authoritative balance or an offline player, use the future from api.readBalance(playerId, coin). To display the balance after a particular write, use its result.balance(). var ranks = api.top(coin, 10, 5); var query = net.momirealms.sparrow.feature.economy.history.EconomyHistoryQuery.search( playerId, coin.id(), BigDecimal.ONE, null, java.time.Duration.ofDays(7)); var firstPage = api.history(query, null, 20); The ranking example skips ten wallets and returns ranks 11 through 15 with their UUIDs and four-decimal balances. Use api.top(coin, limit) to start at rank one with any positive integer limit. Each call reads the current ranking. The history example returns successful changes of at least one unit in either direction over the last seven days. Read page.entries() when the future completes. If page.next() is present, reuse the same query and pass that cursor to fetch the next page.
Use net.momirealms.sparrow.service.highlight.Highlight to show block outlines to local players. The service starts with Sparrow and remains available when the command is disabled.

HighlightSubmission preview = Highlight.builder() .region(first, second, RegionMode.NON_AIR) .color(NamedTextColor.AQUA) .onLeave(player -> menu.closeFor(player)) .onEnd(menu::release) .commit(viewers); Here menu is the caller's shared preview UI. Omit the callbacks if you only need the outline. Commit each builder once, to one Player or a collection. Green is the default color. The outline lasts until removed or until the session ends. Use .duration(Duration.ofSeconds(10)) to expire ten seconds after display, or preview.remove() to cancel at any time, including during preparation. Repeated removal is safe. Target Positions displayed block(block) One block position. blocks(blocks) Distinct positions in one world, including disconnected groups. region(first, second) or OUTLINE The six faces of the inclusive cuboid. region(first, second, RegionMode.NON_AIR) Every non-air block, including fluids and enclosed blocks. region(first, second, RegionMode.EXPOSED_SOLID) Non-passable blocks on the boundary or next to a passable block on any of six sides. Selecting another target replaces the previous selection. The limit is 32768 distinct positions for a block collection, or 32768 blocks of total cuboid volume before filtering. The service samples the region once at submission. Peaceful worlds are unsupported.

preview.result() completes after initial processing. Displayed contains UUID sets for viewers whose display packets were submitted and viewers who were unavailable. Rejected reports an invalid world, Peaceful difficulty, out-of-bounds height, excessive size or an empty target. Cancelled means the session was removed before display. Packet preparation or sending failures complete the stage exceptionally. onLeave(Player) runs once for a viewer who had a visible outline and changes world, respawns or disconnects. Other viewers keep their outline. Returning to the world requires a new submission. onEnd(Runnable) runs once when the entire session releases its resources, including rejection, no viewers, removal, expiry and Sparrow shutdown. If the last viewer leaves, their leave callback runs first. Expiry and explicit removal trigger only the end callback. Both callbacks run outside the session lock, in session order. The executing thread depends on the trigger. An immediately rejected submission can call onEnd before commit returns.

Add the current Sparrow build as a compile dependency and declare your plugin's dependency on Sparrow. Here, player is a local online SparrowPlayer, and logger is your plugin's logger. TeleportSubmission submission = Teleport.builder() .server("lobby") .position("world", 0.5, 64, 0.5) .postProcessor(new PlaySound()) .commit(player) .onResult(result -> result.ifFail(fail -> player.sendTranslatedMessage(fail.reason()))) .onError(error -> logger.log(Level.SEVERE, "Teleport failed", error)); server takes a Sparrow server ID; the local ID uses a local teleport. Cross-server requests require configured Sparrow backends and proxy services. commit also accepts a Bukkit Player. Submit each builder once.

Expression Purpose position(world, x, y, z[, yaw, pitch]) Fixed coordinates. position(TeleportPosition.ofPos(worldLocation)) A saved WorldLocation. position(TeleportPosition.ofPlayer(uuid)) A player on the destination server; also accepts a player name. position(TeleportPosition.rtpBuilder()...build()) A random search within areas. server(...) also accepts Supplier<String> and CompletionStage<String>. Player destinations capture coordinates during preparation; they do not keep tracking movement. Fixed coordinates are used directly. Add FindSafeLoc for a safety check: FindSafeLoc safe = FindSafeLoc.builder() .search(SearchPattern.exact(), SearchPattern.nearby().horizontalRadius(4).up(8).down(8).build()) .rules(PhysicalSafety.builder().build()) .chunks(ChunkPolicy.EXISTING_ONLY) .maxChecks(10_000) .timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(3)) .build(); Teleport.builder() .server("survival") .position("world", 100.5, 64, 100.5) .targetProcessor(safe) .postProcessor(new Invulnerability(5)) .commit(player); SearchPattern provides exact(), nearby() and column(), tried in order. PhysicalSafety checks collisions, support, boundaries and hazards; it rejects water, leaf support and Nether-roof locations by default. EXISTING_ONLY uses generated chunks; ALLOW_GENERATION permits generation. For random teleportation, build a destination: TeleportPosition random = TeleportPosition.rtpBuilder() .areas(RtpArea.builder("world").rectangle(-5000, -5000, 5000, 5000).build()) .nearbyColumns(2, 4, 4) .rules(PhysicalSafety.builder().build()) .chunks(ChunkPolicy.ALLOW_GENERATION) .maxAttempts(32) .maxChecks(10_000) .timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(9)) .build(); Teleport.builder().server("survival").position(random).commit(player); rectangle takes minX, minZ, maxX, maxZ, optionally followed by minY, maxY. Multiple areas may use different worlds on the same destination server. Available scan modes are AUTO, SURFACE, CAVITY_TOP_DOWN and CAVITY_BOTTOM_UP. The example sets the search ranges and budgets explicitly. targetProcessor checks or adjusts coordinates after destination resolution. A custom PositionProcessor returns Accept, Reject or Relocate. postProcessor runs actions in order after arrival; built-ins include PlaySound and Invulnerability.

Attach a condition to prepare the destination while waiting for confirmation or a countdown: CompletableFuture<Void> confirmation = new CompletableFuture<>(); TeleportSubmission pending = Teleport.builder() .server("lobby") .position("world", 0.5, 64, 0.5) .condition(confirmation) .commit(player); Call confirmation.complete(null) to confirm, or pending.cancel() to cancel. Execution waits for every condition to complete normally; a failed or cancelled condition produces Aborted. Only completion status matters: a CompletableFuture<Boolean> completed with false still passes. Entry point Meaning onPrepared(...) Preparation succeeded; exposes the destination without pausing execution. onResult(...) Success, Fail(reason) or Aborted(cause); use ifSuccess, ifFail and ifAborted to handle branches. onError(...) A program error. preparationResult() / result() Observation Futures for composition; do not complete or cancel them yourself. cancel() Cancels only before execution starts; returns true on cancellation and produces Fail(TELEPORT_CANCELLED). commitForget(player) Ignore business results and log program errors. Success reports the completed move without waiting for all post-processors. Callbacks have no player-thread guarantee; schedule entity or world mutations as required by the platform.

context(new TeleportContext()) carries NBT parameters and belongs to the request after submission. Setting TeleportContext.UNSAFE to true lets FindSafeLoc fall back to its input coordinates when the search fails. RTP does not use this fallback. Extension interface Type registry TeleportPosition TeleportPosition.TYPES PositionProcessor PositionProcessor.TYPES PostProcessor PostProcessor.TYPES SafetyRule SafetyRule.TYPES Implement type() and toNbt(), then register a decoder with the corresponding registry's register(type, decoder). Register on the sending server and every possible receiving server. Transfer configuration in NBT; obtain service objects locally. Put restrictions in SafetyRule when a search should continue trying candidates. RTP's testBeforeResolve can check X/Z early and return PASS, REJECT or DEFER; DEFER calls test after resolving Y. A later target processor's rejection does not restart RTP, and relocated coordinates are not rechecked against earlier area restrictions. TeleportRequestEvent and TeleportReadyEvent run on the destination server before resolution and after target processing; both are cancellable. TeleportArriveEvent exposes departure and arrival locations after a cross-server arrival.

A waypoint shows one local player a marker for a target. The viewer sees the marker, the target is the real location, and the anchor is where the marker is drawn. A distant target can have an anchor close to the viewer. Arrival checks and distance labels still use the real target.

Add Sparrow as a compile-time dependency and declare a runtime dependency on the plugin. The entry point is net.momirealms.sparrow.service.waypoint.Waypoint. Call Waypoint.builder().target(target).track(viewer) with a target and a Bukkit Player who has entered play on the local server. Set the label, style, distances and callbacks before calling track. Each call to track(viewer) returns an independent WaypointTracking. Keep both handles when a player tracks a gate and a teammate. Calling stop() on the gate handle ends only the gate session. Repeated calls are safe. Disconnecting the viewer ends all their sessions.

Factory or interface Resolution WaypointTarget.ofPos(world, x, y, z) Tracks fixed coordinates by world name and XYZ. Use ofPos(WorldLocation) for an existing snapshot. WaypointTarget.ofPlayer(uuid), ofPlayer(name) Follows a local player by UUID or exact name. Tracking can resume when they reconnect in the viewer's world. WaypointTarget.ofEntity(uuid) Follows a loaded entity. It becomes unavailable while unloaded and can be found again after loading. WaypointTarget.resolve(viewer) A custom target returns a WorldLocation for this viewer on each refresh, or null while unavailable. Resolution runs on the asynchronous refresh thread. Avoid blocking on external data.

Method Default Meaning followDistance(blocks) 60 blocks Maximum distance from the viewer's eyes to the projected anchor. Accepts a finite positive value. For nearby targets the anchor can coincide with the target. hideWithin(blocks) 0 Hides the whole marker when the distance from the viewer's feet to the real target is at or below this radius. Leaving restores it. Accepts a finite non-negative value. Zero disables radius hiding and arrival/leave callbacks. moveTolerance(blocks) 0.05 blocks Updates an element's position once its displacement from the last sent position exceeds this value. Accepts a finite non-negative value. Zero updates on each position change. Text content can update independently.

All four callbacks receive (viewer, tracking) on the asynchronous refresh thread. The session stays active when the target is lost or the viewer enters the hide radius. Call tracking.stop() inside a callback when that transition should end the session. Callback When it fires onTrack A target is first found in the same world or reacquired after loss. If first found inside the hide radius, this runs before onArrival. onArrival The viewer enters the radius and the marker has been hidden. Staying inside produces only one notification. onLeave The viewer leaves the radius while the target is still available. Display resumes after the callback returns. onLoss A previously tracked target becomes unavailable or the viewer leaves its world. An initial lookup that finds nothing does not trigger it.

Set the style with Waypoint.builder().style(style). The default shows a ◆ marker and distance. Set the name separately with label(Component) on the tracking builder. Tracks can share a style while displaying different names. Option on WaypointStyle.builder() Usage marker(marker) Choose WaypointMarker.text(Component), block(Material) or item(org.bukkit.inventory.ItemStack). Use the marker returned by marker.scale(float) to resize it independently of the label and beam. beam(beam) Adds an optional two-layer beam. Configure materials and dimensions on WaypointBeam.builder() with outer(material, width), inner(material, width) and height(blocks). distanceFormatter(formatter), hideDistance() The default shows whole metres below 1000 blocks and kilometres to one decimal place thereafter. A formatter receives the unrounded distance and returns a component in your chosen font or style. Hiding the distance line keeps the name visible.

Use WaypointStyle.custom(layout) to choose the elements and their arrangement. The service calls WaypointLayout.render(view, elements) on every visible refresh, even when the target is stationary. Declare the whole layout each time. Reuse the same key across frames for each element. Omitting a key removes its element. Use the elements and their container only within the current callback. WaypointView supplies the viewer(), real target(), projected anchor() and optional label(). Use distance() for the distance from the viewer's feet to the target and anchorDistance() for the distance from their eyes to the anchor. The suggested text multiplier readableScale() is 1 within 8 blocks and the anchor distance divided by 8 beyond that. Layout operation Usage Declare elements elements.text(key, component) displays text. item(key, stack) takes a snapshot of an NMS ItemStack. block(key, state) accepts an NMS BlockState, including a specific custom block state. Position and transform position(x, y, z) offsets an element from its anchor or parent socket in world axes, in blocks. translate(x, y, z) offsets it in display space. Set the centre for scale(...) and rotate(...) with pivot(...). Orientation and text billboard(...) sets orientation. Text defaults to CENTER; items and blocks default to FIXED. Text supports alignment(...), lineWidth(pixels), shadow(boolean) and seeThrough(boolean). Attach elements Declare a model-local point with socket(name, x, y, z) on the parent. Call attachTo(parentKey, name) on the child to align it with that point while retaining its own scale. Attachments must be acyclic. If the parent turns with the camera, use the same billboard on the child. visible(false) hides the subtree.

label(Component) takes a prebuilt name. Use a custom layout for a live health reading or placeholder. Keep the sample time, last displayed value and text component per track. Read the data when the sampling interval expires and rebuild the component when its displayed value changes. Continue declaring the element every frame so it follows the target between samples. For a <papi:...> label, resolve MiniMessage with the intended player when the sample is due and reuse the result until the next sample. The placeholder value becomes known only after resolution.

Replace world and the coordinates with the location of your gate. The default style shows a marker, the gate name and its distance. The marker hides within five blocks and returns when the viewer walks away. public final class NorthGate { public static WaypointTracking show(Player viewer) { return Waypoint.builder() .target(WaypointTarget.ofPos("world", 120.5, 70, -31.5)) .label(Component.text("North Gate")) .hideWithin(5) .track(viewer); } }

The marker follows the teammate on every visible refresh. Health is sampled at most once every 500 ms, and a new text component is built only when the displayed whole number changes. Each call to show creates its own layout, so two tracks never share a health reading. public final class TeammateWaypoint { public static WaypointTracking show(Player viewer, Player teammate) { UUID id = teammate.getUniqueId(); return Waypoint.builder() .target(WaypointTarget.ofPlayer(id)) .style(WaypointStyle.custom(new HealthLayout(id))) .track(viewer); } private static final class HealthLayout implements WaypointLayout { private static final long INTERVAL = TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS.toNanos(500); private final UUID teammateId; private long lastRead; private int displayedHealth; private Component healthText; private HealthLayout(UUID teammateId) { this.teammateId = teammateId; } @Override public void render(WaypointView view, WaypointElements elements) { long now = System.nanoTime(); if (this.healthText == null || now - this.lastRead >= INTERVAL) { Player teammate = Bukkit.getPlayer(this.teammateId); if (teammate == null) return; this.lastRead = now; int health = (int) Math.ceil(teammate.getHealth()); if (this.healthText == null || health != this.displayedHealth) { this.displayedHealth = health; this.healthText = Component.text("Teammate · " + health + " HP"); } } elements.text("health", this.healthText) .seeThrough(true) .scale(view.readableScale()); } } }

documents.t: <argument> is required; [argument] is optional. These are the default entry points and permissions. Short commands also accept /sparrow <command> or /spr <command>. Restart after editing commands.yml. [.other] marks branches that additionally require .other when specifying another player. Entity selectors only select local targets; commands with cross-server support also accept a player name from another backend. Default multiword commands use hyphens, as in /set-home. Its permission is sparrow.command.set_home.

Examples use the coin alias /money. The same branches are available under /economy <currency ID>. Use /economy history to search across currencies. Command Purpose Permission /money Show your balance sparrow.command.economy.balance /money balance <player> Inspect a player’s exact balance sparrow.command.economy.inspect /money give <player> <amount> [reason] [-s] Credit a wallet sparrow.command.economy.give /money take <player> <amount> [reason] [-s] Debit a wallet sparrow.command.economy.take /money pay <player> <amount> Pay a player sparrow.command.economy.pay /money top [limit] Open the rich list sparrow.command.economy.top /money history all Browse currency history sparrow.command.economy.history /money history player <player> Filter history by player sparrow.command.economy.history /money history transaction <id> Inspect one transaction sparrow.command.economy.history sparrow.command.economy.pay.offline allows payments to offline players and defaults to OP. History lists accept --min, --max and --within.

Command Purpose Default permission /sparrow reload [--silent] Reload configuration. sparrow.command.admin.reload /sparrow feature-list Open the module management dialog (players only). sparrow.command.admin.feature /sparrow feature-enable <feature> Enable a module immediately without saving its switch. sparrow.command.admin.feature /sparrow feature-disable <feature> Disable a module immediately without saving its switch. sparrow.command.admin.feature Use death_messages as the feature name to manage Death messages. Edit modules.yml to keep module switches after a reload or restart.

Command Purpose Default permission /maintenance [true|false] [--all] [--tag <tag>] Change maintenance mode. sparrow.command.maintenance /max-players [amount] View or change the player limit; -1 restores the original limit. sparrow.command.max_players /kick <targets> [reason] [--silent] Kick players, including across servers. sparrow.command.kick /ban <player|player-ip|ip> <target> [reason] [--time <duration>] [--force] [--silent] Ban an account or IP. sparrow.command.ban /unban <player|player-ip|ip> <target> [--silent] Lift an account or IP ban. sparrow.command.unban /unban-id <id> [--silent] Revoke a ban by record ID. sparrow.command.unban_id /ban-info <id> Open a ban record (players only). sparrow.command.ban_info /ban-history <all|player <player>|ip <ip>> [options] Browse ban history (players only). sparrow.command.ban_history /player-info <name-or-uuid> View player records and ban status. sparrow.command.player_info /player-uuid <name> Look up a player's UUID. sparrow.command.player_uuid /name-history <name-or-uuid> View name history. sparrow.command.name_history /ip-history <player <name>|uuid <uuid>|ip <ip>> View a player's IP history or records for an IP. sparrow.command.ip_history /player-info, /name-history and /ip-history open player-only dialogs. From a profile, the available actions depend on your permissions. You can open name, IP or ban history, or travel to the recorded logout location. Select an IP in the history dialog to see which players used it.

Command Purpose Default permission /give <player> <item> [count] Give vanilla or CraftEngine items, including across servers. sparrow.command.give /heal [player [--value <amount>]] Restore health; hunger and effects are unchanged. sparrow.command.heal[.other] /feed [player [--value <amount>]] Restore food level. sparrow.command.feed[.other] /air <player> [--value <amount>] Set remaining air; omit the value to refill it. sparrow.command.air /fly [player [enabled]] Toggle flight or set it for a named player. sparrow.command.fly[.other] /fly-speed <speed> [player] Set flight speed from -1 to 1. sparrow.command.fly_speed[.other] /walk-speed <speed> [player] Set walking speed from -1 to 1. sparrow.command.walk_speed[.other] /burn <time> [targets] Set entities on fire; durations accept units such as 5s. sparrow.command.burn[.other] /extinguish [targets] Extinguish entities. sparrow.command.extinguish[.other] /smite <targets> [--effect] Strike entities with lightning; --effect is visual only. sparrow.command.smite /look <face <face>|location <x> <y> <z>|entity <entity>> [targets] Change facing direction. sparrow.command.look[.other] /knockback <x> <y> <z> [player] Apply knockback. sparrow.command.knockback[.other] /hat [player] Wear one main-hand item as a hat. sparrow.command.hat[.other] /respawn [player] Respawn a dead player. sparrow.command.respawn[.other] /suicide Kill yourself. sparrow.command.suicide /patrol [targets] Cycle through players for patrol, including across servers. sparrow.command.patrol /force-say <player> <text> Make a local player send a chat message. sparrow.command.force_say /sudo <player> <command> Make a local player execute a command. sparrow.command.sudo

Command Purpose Default permission /world <world> [targets] [--location <x> <y> <z>] [--unsafe] Travel to a world on this server. sparrow.command.world[.other] /top-block [targets] Move to the top of the current block column. sparrow.command.top_block[.other] /tp-offline <player> [target] [--silent] Send yourself or a local target to a player's recorded logout location. sparrow.command.tp_offline /server <server> [targets] Transfer to another backend. sparrow.command.server[.other] /spawn Travel to the configured spawn. sparrow.command.spawn /back [player] [--unsafe] [--silent] Return to the previous teleport departure point. sparrow.command.back[.other] /death-back [player] [--unsafe] [--silent] Return to the last death location. sparrow.command.death-back[.other] /rtp <player> <region> [--silent] Teleport randomly within a configured region. sparrow.command.rtp[.other] /rtp-range <player> <server> <world> <min-radius> <max-radius> [options] Teleport randomly within a specified square range. sparrow.command.rtp_range[.other] /warp <name> [player] Travel to a warp, with support for cross-server players. sparrow.command.warp[.other] /set-warp <name> Create a warp at your position. sparrow.command.set_warp /del-warp <name> Delete a warp. sparrow.command.del_warp /warp-list Open the list of visible warps (players only). sparrow.command.warp_list /edit-warp <name> [rename <new_name>|relocate] View, rename or relocate a warp. sparrow.command.edit_warp /home [name] Travel to your home; player.name selects another owner's home. sparrow.command.home[.other] /set-home [name] Create a home at your position; the default name is home. sparrow.command.set_home /del-home <name> Delete a home; accepts player.name. sparrow.command.del_home[.other] /home-list [owner] Open your or another owner’s home list (players only). sparrow.command.home_list[.other] /edit-home <name> [rename <new_name>|relocate] View, rename or relocate a home; accepts player.name. sparrow.command.edit_home[.other] /sparrow del-all-homes [--player <player>] [--server <server>] [--world <world>] Bulk delete from console; at least one filter, no confirmation. sparrow.command.del_all_homes /tpa <player> Ask to teleport to another player. sparrow.command.tpa /tpa-here <player> Ask another player to teleport to you. sparrow.command.tpa_here /tpa-accept [player] Accept a request; defaults to the most recent one. sparrow.command.tpa_accept /tpa-deny [player] Deny a request; defaults to the most recent one. sparrow.command.tpa_deny /tpa-cancel [player] Cancel an outgoing request; omit the player to cancel all. sparrow.command.tpa_cancel

Command Purpose Default permission /workbench [player] [--title <text>] Open a crafting table. sparrow.command.workbench[.other] /anvil [player] [--title <text>] Open an anvil. sparrow.command.anvil[.other] /grindstone [player] [--title <text>] Open a grindstone. sparrow.command.grindstone[.other] /smithing-table [player] [--title <text>] Open a smithing table. sparrow.command.smithing_table[.other] /stonecutter [player] [--title <text>] Open a stonecutter. sparrow.command.stonecutter[.other] /cartography-table [player] [--title <text>] Open a cartography table. sparrow.command.cartography_table[.other] /enchantment-table [player] [--title <text>] Open an enchanting table. sparrow.command.enchantment_table[.other] /loom [player] [--title <text>] Open a loom. sparrow.command.loom[.other] /ender-chest [player] [--title <text>] Have the player open their own ender chest. sparrow.command.ender_chest[.other] /clear-inv <player> Clear inventory, equipment, cursor and crafting slots. sparrow.command.clear_inv /clear-ender <player> Clear an ender chest. sparrow.command.clear_ender /repair <player> [--slot <slot>] [--value <amount>] Repair an equipment slot; defaults to a full main-hand repair. sparrow.command.repair /repair-all <player> Repair inventory and equipment. sparrow.command.repair_all /item-damage <player> <value> Set main-hand item damage. sparrow.command.item_damage /enchant <player> <enchantment> [level] [--slot <slot>] [--check] Edit an enchantment; negative levels remove it, --check applies vanilla limits. sparrow.command.enchant /item-name [name] [--json] View or edit your main-hand item_name. sparrow.command.item_name /custom-name [name] [--json] View or edit your main-hand custom_name. sparrow.command.custom_name /item-lore editor Open the multiline editor for your main-hand item (players only). sparrow.command.item_lore /item-lore edit --operation <operation> [--player <player>] [--slot <slot>] [--line <line>] [--lore <text>] Edit lore in the selected slot. Defaults to yourself and your main hand. sparrow.command.item_lore[.other] /custom-model-data [value] View or edit the first custom model data float. sparrow.command.custom_model_data /color <color> [player] Dye the main-hand item. sparrow.command.color[.other] /more [amount] [player] [--silent] Replenish or copy the main-hand item. sparrow.command.more /head [source] [amount] [player] [--force] [--silent] Obtain a player head. sparrow.command.head[.other]

Command Purpose Default permission /broadcast <message> [--silent] Broadcast a message across the network. sparrow.command.broadcast /actionbar <targets> <message> [--silent] Send an action bar. sparrow.command.actionbar /title <targets> <fadeIn> <stay> <fadeOut> <message> [--silent] Send a title; durations are in ticks. sparrow.command.title /toast <targets> <type> <item> <message> [--silent] Display an advancement toast. sparrow.command.toast /totem-animation <targets> <item> [--silent] Play a totem animation using the specified item. sparrow.command.totem_animation /clear-chat [player] Clear chat; defaults to everyone on this server. sparrow.command.clear_chat /demo [player] Show the demo screen. sparrow.command.demo /credits [player] Show the credits. sparrow.command.credits /distance [--max-distance <distance>] [--disable-marker] Measure the distance along your line of sight. sparrow.command.distance /highlight [targets] [options] Highlight a region's blocks. sparrow.command.highlight

ban-history accepts --active, --within <duration> and --operator <name>. Turn pages in the dialog. See Bans. rtp-range accepts --center-x, --center-z, --min-y, --max-y and --silent; see Random teleport. The rename and relocate branches of edit-home and edit-warp require .rename and .relocate appended to the base permission. Editing another owner's home also requires .other. See the command options and the Highlight API. Messages and item text use MiniMessage. Use <papi:placeholder> or <papi:placeholder:default> for PlaceholderAPI. item-name and custom-name accept JSON with --json.

In /item-lore editor, each line is one lore entry. Clear the editor and save to remove all lore. To append a line, use /item-lore edit --operation insert --lore <gold>Treasure. Line numbers start at 1. Only insert can omit --line. The other operations are edit, remove, up and down. Both insert and edit require MiniMessage text in --lore. From console, specify a local online player with --player. Editing another player requires sparrow.command.item_lore.other.

Permission Purpose sparrow.bypass.maintenance Allow entry during maintenance. Configured elevator use_permission Grant this node to ride that block type. Empty by default, allowing everyone. sparrow.bypass.player_limit Allow entry when full. sparrow.bypass.patrol Exclude from patrol. sparrow.notify.ban Receive ban and unban notices. sparrow.bypass.tpa_cooldown Skip request and denial cooldowns. sparrow.home.limit.<amount> / sparrow.home.limit.unlimited Override the home limit. sparrow.warp.use.<lowercase-name> Allow access to a warp when permission-restrict is enabled. sparrow.back.staff / sparrow.back.vip Default Back cooldown and warmup overrides. sparrow.deathback.staff / sparrow.deathback.vip Default DeathBack cooldown and warmup overrides. sparrow.rtp.staff / sparrow.rtp.vip Default RTP cooldown and warmup overrides. sparrow.tpa.staff / sparrow.tpa.vip Default TPA teleport cooldown and warmup overrides. sparrow.home.teleport.staff / sparrow.home.teleport.vip Default Home cooldown and warmup overrides. sparrow.warp.teleport.staff / sparrow.warp.teleport.vip Default Warp cooldown and warmup overrides. sparrow.spawn.staff Default Spawn cooldown and warmup override. Teleport override permissions are configurable in each feature's teleport-options.overrides; RTP region permissions use regions.<name>.permission.

Online time guide Command Purpose Permission /online-time Open overview sparrow.command.online_time.report /online-time new [date] New registrations sparrow.command.online_time.report /online-time retention Exact-day retention sparrow.command.online_time.report /online-time player <player> Player records sparrow.command.online_time.report /online-time calendar <player> [month] Records for a month sparrow.command.online_time.report

Module back · Configuration features/back.yaml /back returns to the previous departure point; /death-back returns to the last death location. Both support cross-server destinations. A named traveler must be on this server.

Command Purpose Default permission /back [player] [--unsafe] [--silent] Return to the previous teleport departure point. sparrow.command.back[.other] /death-back [player] [--unsafe] [--silent] Return to the last death location. sparrow.command.death-back[.other]
Permission Purpose sparrow.back.staff / sparrow.back.vip Default Back cooldown and warmup overrides. sparrow.deathback.staff / sparrow.deathback.vip Default DeathBack cooldown and warmup overrides.

--unsafe allows the original coordinates when no safe location is found; --silent hides command feedback. back.teleport-causes records COMMAND and PLUGIN by default. back.join-grace-seconds ignores ordinary teleports during the first 3 seconds after joining. deathback.record-death controls recording of new death locations. Configure their cooldowns and warmups separately under back.teleport-options and deathback.teleport-options; see Teleport options.
# Ignore ordinary teleports for this many seconds after joining back: join-grace-seconds: 3
Module ban · Configuration features/ban.yml Ban accounts, IPs or IP ranges across servers, with a persistent history.

Command Purpose Default permission /ban <player|player-ip|ip> <target> [reason] [--time <duration>] [--force] [--silent] Ban an account or IP. sparrow.command.ban /unban <player|player-ip|ip> <target> [--silent] Lift an account or IP ban. sparrow.command.unban /unban-id <id> [--silent] Revoke a ban by record ID. sparrow.command.unban_id /ban-info <id> Open a ban record (players only). sparrow.command.ban_info /ban-history <all|player <player>|ip <ip>> [options] Browse ban history (players only). sparrow.command.ban_history
Permission Purpose sparrow.notify.ban Receive ban and unban notices.

/ban player Steve griefing --time 7d /ban player-ip Steve /ban ip 192.0.2.* unwanted traffic /ban-history player Steve --active /unban-id 12 player bans an account. player-ip bans the player's last recorded IP without adding an account ban. ip accepts an address or range. Omit --time for a permanent ban; --force replaces an active ban for the same target. --silent hides notices and success feedback. Turn pages in the dialog. History filters are --active, --within <duration> and --operator <name>. sparrow.notify.ban receives ban and unban notices. With permission for /ban-info, select a history entry to open its details. With permission for /unban-id, revoke an active ban from its details and choose whether to silence notices before confirming. Add common reasons to reason-presets; an exact preset name expands to its text. Notification sounds use notify-ban-sound and notify-unban-sound. Players can give the ban ID on the disconnect screen to an administrator. For the record shown here, use /ban-info 21.
# Example: expand grief to Griefing when entered as the reason reason-presets: grief: "Griefing"

Module death_messages · Configuration features/death_messages.yml Customize player death announcements with complete sentences for each vanilla death situation. Messages support MiniMessage, player hover text and the weapon details supplied by Minecraft. Announcements can stay on the current server or be broadcast across the network. Minecraft's death attribution is preserved, including deaths while escaping an attacker and assisted falls. The death screen keeps its existing message. When death announcements are already hidden by the server or another plugin, Sparrow leaves them hidden.

The module is enabled by default. Its persistent switch is in modules.yml: death_messages: true Command Purpose Default permission /spr feature-enable death_messages Enable rewriting on this server immediately. sparrow.command.admin.feature /spr feature-disable death_messages Stop rewriting on this server immediately. sparrow.command.admin.feature /spr reload Apply configuration changes. sparrow.command.admin.reload The enable and disable commands change the current state without saving the switch. Edit modules.yml to keep the choice after a reload or restart. If the DeathMessages configuration is invalid, reloading fails for this module and its last valid settings remain active. There are no feature-specific commands or permissions. Disabling this module stops rewriting deaths that happen on this server; players may still receive cross-server announcements from other servers. See Commands and permissions for module management.

The generated file contains 101 default rules. The example below shows only a few rules and customized display text; edit the generated file to keep the other death situations covered. broadcast: false disabled_worlds: [] anti-spam: enabled: true interval: 30s max-messages: 3 show-to-victim: true format: '<dark_gray>☠ <gray><arg:message>' display: player: name: '<white><arg:display_name>' hover: - '<gray>Player: <white><arg:name>' - '<gray>Server: <white><arg:server>' mob: name: '<yellow><arg:entity_name>' fallback: - '<arg:original>' rules: - id: player_with_weapon message_key: death.attack.player.item broadcast: true messages: - '<arg:attacker> killed <arg:victim> using <arg:weapon>' - '<arg:victim> was defeated by <arg:attacker> using <arg:weapon>' - id: lava_escape message_key: death.attack.lava.player messages: - '<arg:victim> jumped into lava while escaping <arg:attacker>' - id: ladder_fall message_key: death.fell.accident.ladder messages: - '<arg:victim> fell off a ladder'

Field Meaning id A nonempty, unique name for the rule. message_key The exact vanilla death-message key, including capitalization and any suffix. broadcast Optional override for the public broadcast setting. disabled_worlds Optional replacement for the public disabled-world list. messages Required list of complete sentences. One entry is selected randomly for each death. If several rules have the same message_key, the first one wins. Keys are matched exactly: a rule for death.attack.player does not also match death.attack.player.item. All recipients share the same randomly selected sentence. Each sentence can place the victim, attacker and weapon wherever you want. messages: [] hides that death situation, including the outer format. A selected empty string also hides the announcement. A rule that hides an announcement does not continue to another rule or use fallback. Unmatched keys use a random entry from fallback, together with the public broadcast and disabled_worlds settings. The default fallback, <arg:original>, keeps the vanilla death message inside your outer format. Set fallback: [] to hide unmatched situations. Some useful vanilla keys are: message_key Situation death.attack.player Killed by a player. death.attack.player.item Killed by a player, with weapon details supplied by Minecraft. death.attack.mob Killed by a mob. death.attack.arrow.item Shot, with weapon details supplied by Minecraft. death.attack.lava Died in lava. death.attack.lava.player Died in lava while escaping an attacker. death.fell.accident.ladder Fell off a ladder. death.fell.assist.item An attacker caused a fatal fall, with weapon details. death.fell.finish Fell and was finished off by an attacker. death.attack.badRespawnPoint.message A bed or respawn-anchor explosion, with the vanilla death-reason link. The .player suffix is part of Minecraft's key naming; the attributed attacker can also be a mob. Use the generated rules as the reference for the remaining keys.

Public setting Default Meaning broadcast false false announces locally; true announces across the Sparrow network. disabled_worlds [] Hide deaths occurring in these worlds. Names are matched exactly on the server where the death occurs. A rule inherits either setting when it omits that field. An explicit value replaces the public value: broadcast: false overrides a public broadcast: true; false still announces locally. disabled_worlds: [] clears the disabled-world restriction for that rule. A nonempty rule list replaces the public world list completely; the lists are not merged. For example, this configuration normally broadcasts across the network and hides deaths in lobby. The weapon rule announces locally and also permits announcements for deaths in lobby: broadcast: true disabled_worlds: [lobby] rules: - id: local_weapon_kill message_key: death.attack.player.item broadcast: false disabled_worlds: [] messages: - '<arg:victim> was killed by <arg:attacker> using <arg:weapon>' These choices come from the server where the death occurs. A disabled world hides that announcement for everyone, including players on other servers; it does not filter recipients by their current world. Receiving servers use the selected announcement and do not choose another rule or sentence. For cross-server announcements, use Sparrow versions that support this feature on the receiving backends and configure the network as described in the Introduction. Player and weapon hover details are retained across servers.

Setting Purpose format Outer chat format. <arg:message> inserts the selected sentence. display.player.name Display format shared by the victim and player attackers. display.player.hover Lines shown when hovering over a displayed player. [] adds no custom hover text. display.mob.name Mob name display. <arg:entity_name> preserves custom names and vanilla translated names. Use these arguments in rule messages, fallback text and the outer format: Argument Value <arg:victim> The victim, with the configured player display. <arg:attacker> The attacker attributed by Minecraft, with the configured player or mob display. Available only in applicable situations. <arg:weapon> The weapon name and item hover supplied by the vanilla message. Available only in applicable .item situations. <arg:death_reason> The special reason link for a bed or respawn-anchor explosion. <arg:original> The complete vanilla death message, with its original names and hover details. <arg:server> The ID of the server where the death occurred. <arg:world> The name of the world where the death occurred. <arg:x>, <arg:y>, <arg:z> Death location as block coordinates. <arg:message_key> The vanilla key selected for this death. attacker, weapon and death_reason are not available for every death. Use them in matching rules, or supply a default such as <arg:weapon:'unknown weapon'> in a shared template. Weapon availability follows Minecraft's death message; holding a weapon does not guarantee that the message supplies it. All default .item rules include <arg:weapon>. Inside display.player, <arg:name> is that player's account name and <arg:display_name> is their display name. <arg:server> remains the server where the death occurred. PlaceholderAPI is optional. With it installed, use <papi:placeholder> or <papi:placeholder:default>, rather than %placeholder%: In display.player.name and display.player.hover, PAPI refers to the displayed player: the victim for their name, or the player attacker for theirs. In messages, fallback and format, PAPI refers to each recipient. For example, <papi:player_name> shows the viewer's name, including on another server. Mob display text has no player-specific PAPI context.

Setting Default Meaning anti-spam.enabled true Limit repeated announcements from the same player. anti-spam.interval 30s Positive duration with units, such as 30s or 1m. anti-spam.max-messages 3 Positive maximum number of normal announcements in that interval. anti-spam.show-to-victim true Send excess announcements only to the victim. false hides them from everyone. With the defaults, the first three announcements from a player within the preceding 30 seconds are sent normally. Further deaths in that window are shown only to that player and are not broadcast across servers. Excess deaths still count, so continued deaths can keep the limit active until older deaths leave the window. Deaths hidden by the server, another plugin, a disabled-world rule or an empty message do not count. show-to-victim does not override those hiding rules. Limits apply separately on each server and reset when the player leaves that server or the module is disabled.
Set economy: true in modules.yml and restart. Use /money or /coins for coins and /points for points. Each wallet starts at zero for each currency.

Examples use the coin alias /money. The same branches are available under /economy <currency ID>. Use /economy history to search across currencies. Command Purpose Permission /money Show your balance sparrow.command.economy.balance /money balance <player> Inspect a player’s exact balance sparrow.command.economy.inspect /money give <player> <amount> [reason] [-s] Credit a wallet sparrow.command.economy.give /money take <player> <amount> [reason] [-s] Debit a wallet sparrow.command.economy.take /money pay <player> <amount> Pay a player sparrow.command.economy.pay /money top [limit] Open the rich list sparrow.command.economy.top /money history all Browse currency history sparrow.command.economy.history /money history player <player> Filter history by player sparrow.command.economy.history /money history transaction <id> Inspect one transaction sparrow.command.economy.history sparrow.command.economy.pay.offline allows payments to offline players and defaults to OP. History lists accept --min, --max and --within.
Economy configuration files plugins/Sparrow modules.yml features economy economy.yml currencies coin.yml points.yml

vault: enabled: true # Enable the integration when Vault is installed. currency: "coin" # Use the currency file name without .yml. history: retention-days: 90 # Days from the transaction date; 0 keeps records indefinitely. page-size: 15 # History rows per page; minimum 1. With Vault installed, shops and other Vault integrations charge and credit the currency selected by vault.currency. Enter its file ID, such as coin. History retention is measured from the transaction date. Set history.retention-days to 0 to keep records indefinitely. history.page-size sets the number of rows per history page and must be at least 1.

display: name: "金币" # Currency name shown to players. symbol: "￥" # Shown wherever the template uses <symbol>. format: "<gold><amount> <name></gold>" # Full amount format. short-format: "<amount> <name>" # Compact format using K, M or B. group-thousands: true # Group digits in formatted amounts. commands: aliases: [money, coins] # Command names without the slash. balance: precision: 2 # Use 0 to 2; 2 displays two decimal places. transfer: enabled: true # Allow player payments with pay. allow-offline-recipient: false # When false, ordinary players can pay recipients online on any backend. permission: "" # Leave empty to require no additional payment permission.

display: name: "点券" # Currency name shown to players. symbol: "★" # Shown wherever the template uses <symbol>. format: "<aqua><amount> <name></aqua>" # Full amount format. short-format: "<amount> <name>" # Compact format using K, M or B. group-thousands: true # Group digits in formatted amounts. commands: aliases: [points] # Command names without the slash. balance: precision: 0 # Display whole numbers; wallets retain four decimals. transfer: enabled: false # Disable player transfers; admins can still credit or debit wallets. allow-offline-recipient: false # When false, ordinary players can pay recipients online on any backend.

Edit currency files under plugins/Sparrow/features/economy/currencies/. The file name is the currency ID. To rename coins for players, edit display.name in coin.yml. Set command names in commands.aliases. Both display.format and display.short-format accept <amount>, <name> and <symbol>. balance.precision accepts 0 through 2. At precision 2, a balance of 123.4993 displays as 123.49. transfer.enabled controls player transfers. Coins allow them by default and points disable them. Set transfer.permission to require an additional permission. With transfer.allow-offline-recipient off (the default), players can still pay someone online on another backend. Administrators can credit or debit offline wallets. Online targets receive a notice unless the administrator appends --silent or -s.

/money top shows the top 50 positive balances across the network, including offline players. Request 1–1000 wallets, ten per page. Reopen the dialog to refresh the ranking. Use /money history player Alex --min 10 --within 7d to see Alex’s coin transactions of at least 10 over the past seven days. Open a transfer to see the payer and recipient. Returning restores the filtered page. In features/economy/economy.yml, history.page-size defaults to 15 and history.retention-days to 90. Use /economy history all to include every player and currency. Select a row to inspect that transaction.

These examples use the default coin configuration and a wallet balance of 12345.6789. Use the placeholders for a player online on the local backend. An offline player or a wallet that is not ready returns empty text. Placeholder Output Example %sparroweco_balance_coin% Plain number at the currency’s display precision, without grouping 12345.67 %sparroweco_integer_balance_coin% Rounded down to a whole number 12345 %sparroweco_formatted_balance_coin% Plain text from display.format 12,345.67 金币 %sparroweco_short_balance_coin% Plain text from display.short-format, abbreviated with K, M or B 12.34K 金币 Replace the final coin with points for points, for example %sparroweco_balance_points%. In Sparrow MiniMessage text, write <papi:sparroweco_formatted_balance_coin>. Use the percent-delimited form in other plugins that accept PlaceholderAPI placeholders. Commands and permissions · Economy API

Module elevator · Configuration features/elevator.yaml Place iron blocks at the same X and Z on two floors in the same world. Stand on the lower block and jump to go up. Stand on the upper block and start sneaking to go down. Holding sneak moves you down just one floor. Building an elevator requires only the usual permission to place blocks. Each ride goes to the nearest block with the same ID in the chosen direction. Solid floors and other elevator types can lie between the stops. The player lands in the center of the target block on its top surface and keeps their viewing direction. If the nearest matching floor is obstructed, the player stays on the original floor even if another floor is clear. Without permission, a clear landing or a matching floor within range, the player can jump or sneak normally. There is no message or sound. A successful ride preserves the existing /back location.

The default file enables only iron blocks. This example adds a custom elevator. Replace smc:lanzi/tiancai with an ID from your CraftEngine pack. elevators: "minecraft:iron_block": max_distance: 64 # Maximum vertical distance between stops use_permission: "" "smc:lanzi/tiancai": max_distance: 32 use_permission: "sparrow.elevator.tiancai" sound: key: minecraft:block.amethyst_block.chime volume: 0.8 pitch: 1.2 Setting Default Meaning max_distance 64 Maximum difference in Y between consecutive floors. Use a positive integer. The limit is inclusive, so Y=20 and Y=84 connect at the default distance. use_permission "" Empty allows everyone to ride. Otherwise, grant the configured node to the players who may use this elevator type. sound Omitted Only the rider hears it, after a successful trip in either direction. Set key to the sound ID. volume and pitch both default to 1.0. Run /spr reload after editing. When upgrading an old elevator-blocks list, Sparrow creates one entry per block and copies its distance and permission.

Install CraftEngine on the backend to use custom floors. Without it, Sparrow skips custom entries with a console warning and vanilla elevators still work. Sparrow resolves the IDs when CraftEngine loads or reloads its resources. Different states of the same custom block connect. An unknown ID in a loaded pack is a configuration error.
Module head · Configuration features/head.yml Get a head from a player name or UUID. Omit the source to get your own head.
Command Purpose Default permission /head [source] [amount] [player] [--force] [--silent] Obtain a player head. sparrow.command.head[.other]

/head Notch /head Notch 16 Steve --force Amounts range from 1 to 6400. --force refreshes profile data. By default, Sparrow tries online player textures before the API. Source order, cache settings and endpoints are configurable.
# Try the online skin first, then the configured API source-order: [online, api]

Configure the command switch, permission and aliases in commands.yml. Plugins can also use the Highlight API. Show block outlines to selected viewers without changing real blocks. Omitting targets shows them to online players in that world. Command Purpose Default permission /highlight [targets] [options] Highlight a region's blocks. sparrow.command.highlight /highlight @s --from 0 64 0 --to 5 68 5 --highlight-color green --highlight-duration 20 Without coordinates, select two points interactively: left-click records your position; right-click records the clicked block. Run the command again without coordinates to cancel selection. Option Purpose --from, --to Endpoints; provide both. --world <world> World; required from console. --highlight-duration <seconds> / -d Duration from 0 to 300 seconds. --highlight-color <color> / -c A named color, such as green or red. --solid-only Show solid blocks exposed to passable neighbors or the selection boundary. --selection-timeout <seconds> Time allowed to select both points, at least 1 second. --silent / -s Hide command feedback. Defaults are a green outline, 30 seconds of display, a 32768-block limit and a 30-second selection timeout. Peaceful worlds are not supported.
Module home · Configuration features/home.yml Save personal destinations and return to them across servers.

Command Purpose Default permission /home [name] Travel to your home; player.name selects another owner's home. sparrow.command.home[.other] /set-home [name] Create a home at your position; the default name is home. sparrow.command.set_home /del-home <name> Delete a home; accepts player.name. sparrow.command.del_home[.other] /home-list [owner] Open your or another owner’s home list (players only). sparrow.command.home_list[.other] /edit-home <name> [rename <new_name>|relocate] View, rename or relocate a home; accepts player.name. sparrow.command.edit_home[.other] /sparrow del-all-homes [--player <player>] [--server <server>] [--world <world>] Bulk delete from console; at least one filter, no confirmation. sparrow.command.del_all_homes

Permission Purpose sparrow.home.limit.<amount> / sparrow.home.limit.unlimited Override the home limit. sparrow.home.teleport.staff / sparrow.home.teleport.vip Default Home cooldown and warmup overrides. sparrow.command.edit_home.rename Rename a home sparrow.command.edit_home.relocate Relocate a home

/set-home mine /home mine /home Steve.mine /home-list Steve Without a name, /home prefers default-name, then your only home. If several homes exist and none matches the default, it opens the list. /set-home does not overwrite an existing name. Use player.name to visit, delete or edit another owner's home, with the corresponding .other permission. home-list takes the owner's name directly. The rename and relocate branches of edit-home also need .rename and .relocate. del-all-homes is console-only and deletes immediately using the intersection of all supplied filters. Players can open home details from the list or with /edit-home <name>. The dialog offers travel, rename, relocate and delete according to permissions. Relocation and deletion from the dialog require confirmation. The default limit is 3 homes. sparrow.home.limit.<amount> overrides max-homes; sparrow.home.limit.unlimited removes the limit. See Teleport options for teleport behavior.

Requires a local online player with a loaded home list. Use <papi:sparrowhome_count> in Sparrow text. Placeholder Result %sparrowhome_count% Number of saved homes %sparrowhome_limit% Home limit, or -1 for unlimited %sparrowhome_remaining% Available slots, or -1 for unlimited %sparrowhome_list% Names sorted and separated by a comma and space
# Prefer home when no name is given; allow three homes per player default-name: home max-homes: 3
Module maintenance · Configuration features/maintenance.yml Block ordinary players from joining during maintenance and show a BossBar to online players.
Command Purpose Default permission /maintenance [true|false] [--all] [--tag <tag>] Change maintenance mode. sparrow.command.maintenance
Permission Purpose sparrow.bypass.maintenance Allow entry during maintenance.

/maintenance true /maintenance false --all /maintenance true --tag survival With no arguments, toggle maintenance on this server; use true or false to set it explicitly. --all targets online network servers; --tag selects servers by tag. sparrow.bypass.maintenance allows entry during maintenance. active stores the maintenance state. boss-bar.enabled controls the bar; its color and style are configured under boss-bar.
# Show the maintenance bar to online players boss-bar: enabled: true

Module online_time · Configuration features/online_time.yml Track daily playtime, daily active players, new registrations and retention. AFK time counts. Timing starts when a player enters the game and continues until disconnection. Time before collection began is not recovered. New players are identified by their first Sparrow profile registration, not by the date this module was enabled.

All report commands are in-game only and use sparrow.command.online_time.report by default. Command Purpose /online-time Open the daily activity overview. /online-time new [date] List players registered on a date; defaults to today. Use YYYY-MM-DD. /online-time retention Open exact-day new-player retention. /online-time player <player> Open the player's records for the current month. /online-time calendar <player> [month] Open the same records page, optionally for YYYY-MM. Examples: /online-time new 2026-11-01 and /online-time calendar Catnies 2026-10. Player names can refer to offline players with existing profiles. Dates and months cannot be in the future. The command configuration key is online_time_report.

time-zone: Asia/Shanghai New configurations use Asia/Shanghai. Omit the setting or leave it blank to use the system time zone. Restart the server after changing it. Participating network servers should use the same time zone. Days follow calendar dates in this zone. Weeks start on Monday; months start on the first day. Sessions spanning midnight or a month boundary, including AFK sessions, are divided between their respective dates without requiring a reconnect. Changing the zone does not redistribute previously recorded daily totals.

Each page shows 14 dates, newest first. Use previous, next, first and last page buttons. Column Definition Active players Distinct players with positive online time that day. Registrations Players first registered that day, independently of whether they have recorded playtime. Total time Combined online time for all players that day. Average Total time divided by active players; — when nobody was active. Click a registration count to open that day's new-player list. The retention link in the header opens the retention report. Reports show saved records: additional online time is normally saved every minute and on departure, rather than refreshed every second. Today's provisional data is marked *.

Columns show player name, registration time, first-day playtime and active days. First-day time covers only the registration date. Active days count dates with positive online time within the reporting range and need not be consecutive. Use previous, next, first and last page buttons to browse players, and the previous-day and next-day buttons to change registration dates. Click a player name to open their records. When following a link between reports, the back button returns to the source page.

player and calendar open the same page. The header shows first registration, online time and active days for the selected month, plus cumulative online time and active days. The daily table shows eight dates per page in ascending order. Daily time covers that date. Cumulative time and active days run from the beginning of available records through the row's date, rather than only the current page or month. Dates with no playtime are also listed; today is marked *. Previous and next page browse within the month. Previous and next month open the first page of the target month. Month-start and today buttons provide shortcuts. Future dates are not shown.

Each page shows 14 registration dates, with D1, D2, D3, D4, D5, D7 and D14 columns. Registration day is D0. DN = players in the registration cohort with online time on the Nth calendar day after registration / all players in that cohort. For example, if 100 players registered on November 1 and 20 were active on November 8, D7 is 20%. Only the specified date counts. Consecutive activity is not required, and missing dates between visits are not treated as retained. D3 can therefore exceed D2. Percentages are colored by value. Hover to see the observation date and counts. Observations for today carry *. Future dates, dates not fully covered by collection, and empty cohorts display — with an explanation on hover. The page total weights each column by eligible cohort sizes, excludes observations still in progress today, and does not simply average percentages. Click a registration date to open its new-player list.

Install PlaceholderAPI to use these placeholders; no separate expansion download is required. Period Readable duration Whole seconds Today %sparrowtime_today% %sparrowtime_today_seconds% This week %sparrowtime_week% %sparrowtime_week_seconds% This month %sparrowtime_month% %sparrowtime_month_seconds% All time %sparrowtime_total% %sparrowtime_total_seconds% In Sparrow text, use MiniMessage tags such as <papi:sparrowtime_today>. The target player is supplied by the plugin requesting the placeholder. For players online on this server, values include time not yet saved. The first offline lookup waits for records and may briefly delay the result. Values for players online on another server are not guaranteed to update live: continuous queries may keep showing an earlier value until the player joins or leaves. Do not use this as a live cross-server timer. Disabled collection or a player whose records are not ready may produce empty text.
Module patrol · Configuration features/patrol.yml Cycle through players across the network by teleporting to them. Omit the target to rotate through eligible players.
Command Purpose Default permission /patrol [targets] Cycle through players for patrol, including across servers. sparrow.command.patrol
Permission Purpose sparrow.bypass.patrol Exclude from patrol.
# Skip spectators when selecting a patrol target skip-spectators: true
Module player_limit · Configuration features/player_limit.yml Change this server's player limit at runtime. Command changes are saved.
Command Purpose Default permission /max-players [amount] View or change the player limit; -1 restores the original limit. sparrow.command.max_players
Permission Purpose sparrow.bypass.player_limit Allow entry when full.
# Restore the previous limit; 0 sets a zero-player limit max-players: -1 Disabling the module also restores the original limit.
Module quick-shulker · Configuration features/quick-shulker.yml Hold a shulker box, sneak and right-click the air. The off hand is supported by default; the main hand takes priority.

require-sneaking: true # Require sneaking to open the box allow-offhand: true title: '<arg:hover_name>' disabled-worlds: [] <arg:hover_name> uses the box's item name. List restricted worlds in disabled-worlds.
Module rtp · Configuration features/rtp.yml Find a safe location within a region, including on another backend. The traveler must be on this server.

Command Purpose Default permission /rtp <player> <region> [--silent] Teleport randomly within a configured region. sparrow.command.rtp[.other] /rtp-range <player> <server> <world> <min-radius> <max-radius> [options] Teleport randomly within a specified square range. sparrow.command.rtp_range[.other]
Permission Purpose sparrow.rtp.staff / sparrow.rtp.vip Default RTP cooldown and warmup overrides. regions.<name>.permission Configurable permission to enter this region

regions: wild: server: survival permission: sparrow.rtp.wild # Permission required for this example region area: world: - x: [-5000, 5000] z: [-5000, 5000] /rtp Steve wild /rtp-range Steve survival world 500 5000 --center-x 0 --center-z 0 Omit server to use this server; omit permission for unrestricted region access. A region can contain multiple worlds and rectangles. Add y: [60, 120] to a rectangle to limit feet height. rtp-range uses a square ring, or a full square when the minimum radius is 0. The center defaults to (0, 0); provide --min-y and --max-y together. Both commands share the RTP cooldown and accept --silent / -s. See Teleport options for cooldowns and warmups, and Landing rules for destination selection.
Module spawn · Configuration features/spawn.yml Travel to the configured spawn, including on another backend. The command is unavailable until a destination is configured.
Command Purpose Default permission /spawn Travel to the configured spawn. sparrow.command.spawn
Permission Purpose sparrow.spawn.staff Default Spawn cooldown and warmup override.

destination: server: lobby # Use the destination backend server ID world: world x: 0.5 y: 64 z: 0.5 yaw: 0 pitch: 0 teleport-options: cooldown: 5m warmup: duration: 0s Configure the destination on each server and run /spr reload. Spawn uses the exact coordinates without a safe-location search. Spawn supports cooldowns, warmups and permission overrides. Its warmup fields use hyphens, such as cancel-on-move and cancel-on-damage.

The respawn section decides where players respawn after death, with priority rules that also work across servers. When a player clicks Respawn, Sparrow picks the first rule that matches the death world and the player's permissions (or default-targets if none matches) and tries its targets in order. The first available target wins. If no target is available, vanilla respawn takes over. Players land on the center of the target block. Hardcore mode and leaving the End always use vanilla respawn. Works on Paper and Folia, both on the server where the player dies and on the server where the player respawns.

A target on another server moves the still-dead player there, and the player respawns on arrival. The death state, such as health and the experience settlement from death, must be synced between servers by another plugin, such as SparrowSync. Without such a plugin, the player arrives with the target server's local data.

With record-personal-point: true, sleeping in a bed or setting a respawn anchor is recorded as a shared personal respawn point, used by the bed and anchor targets on any server. Vanilla respawn points set before enabling are not imported; players need to sleep in a bed or use an anchor again.

Key Purpose default-targets Targets used when no rule matches. rules[].id Rule name, required and unique. rules[].worlds Optional list of death worlds. Omit for any world. rules[].permissions Optional list of permissions; any one is enough. Omit for no requirement. rules[].targets Required, same format as default-targets. Rules are checked in order and the first match wins. When worlds and permissions are both set, both must match. If none of the matching rule's targets is available, vanilla respawn takes over without trying later rules or default-targets. Each target is a map. type is required. worlds and permissions can also be set on a single target, which is skipped unless they match. Other keys are options of the target type. Type Destination Options bed Shared personal bed, may be on another server. Skipped if the bed is gone or obstructed. — anchor Shared personal respawn anchor. Skipped without charge; one charge is used after respawning. — spawn The /spawn destination of this file. Skipped if not set. — world_spawn Spawn point of a world on this server. world: optional, defaults to the death world server_spawn Spawn point of this server's default respawn world. — location Fixed coordinates, no safe-location search. server: optional, defaults to this server; world, x, y, z: required; yaw, pitch: optional, default 0 home A home of the player. Requires the Home module. name: optional. If omitted, the default home is tried first, then the other homes by name warp A warp. Requires the Warp module; the player must be allowed to use it. name: required Targets on offline servers or unloaded worlds are skipped. Types registered by other plugins are written as namespace:type.

respawn: enabled: true record-personal-point: true default-targets: - type: bed - type: anchor - type: world_spawn rules: - id: nether # Nether deaths prefer the respawn anchor worlds: - world_nether targets: - type: anchor - type: bed - type: world_spawn world: world - id: home_respawn # Players with this permission fall back to their home permissions: - sparrow.respawn.home # Any permission node you choose targets: - type: bed - type: anchor - type: home - type: world_spawn - id: lobby_fallback # Everyone else respawns on the lobby server targets: - type: bed - type: location server: lobby world: world x: 0.5 y: 64 z: 0.5 enabled is false by default. The generated features/spawn.yml lists every key and target type in its comments. Run /spr reload after editing.
Module tpa · Configuration features/tpa.yml Send, accept or decline player-to-player teleport requests across servers.

Command Purpose Default permission /tpa <player> Ask to teleport to another player. sparrow.command.tpa /tpa-here <player> Ask another player to teleport to you. sparrow.command.tpa_here /tpa-accept [player] Accept a request; defaults to the most recent one. sparrow.command.tpa_accept /tpa-deny [player] Deny a request; defaults to the most recent one. sparrow.command.tpa_deny /tpa-cancel [player] Cancel an outgoing request; omit the player to cancel all. sparrow.command.tpa_cancel
Permission Purpose sparrow.bypass.tpa_cooldown Skip request and denial cooldowns. sparrow.tpa.staff / sparrow.tpa.vip Default TPA teleport cooldown and warmup overrides.

expire-seconds: 60 request-cooldown-seconds: 10 deny-cooldown-seconds: 120 # Seconds to wait before asking the same player after a denial Requests expire after 60 seconds by default, with 10 seconds between requests and 120 seconds before requesting the same player after a denial. sparrow.bypass.tpa_cooldown skips both request cooldowns. After acceptance, teleport-options applies to the actual traveler. Its teleport cooldown is separate from request intervals; see Teleport options.

Module warp · Configuration features/warp.yml Named destinations shared across your Sparrow servers. Players can open details from /warp-list or /edit-warp <name> to travel, rename, relocate or delete, subject to permissions. Relocation and deletion from the dialog require confirmation.

Command Purpose Default permission /warp <name> [player] Travel to a warp, with support for cross-server players. sparrow.command.warp[.other] /set-warp <name> Create a warp at your position. sparrow.command.set_warp /del-warp <name> Delete a warp. sparrow.command.del_warp /warp-list Open the list of visible warps (players only). sparrow.command.warp_list /edit-warp <name> [rename <new_name>|relocate] View, rename or relocate a warp. sparrow.command.edit_warp

Permission Purpose sparrow.warp.use.<lowercase-name> Allow access to a warp when permission-restrict is enabled. sparrow.warp.teleport.staff / sparrow.warp.teleport.vip Default Warp cooldown and warmup overrides. sparrow.command.edit_warp.rename Rename a warp sparrow.command.edit_warp.relocate Relocate a warp

/set-warp market /warp market /edit-warp market relocate Creation and relocation require a player. /set-warp does not overwrite an existing name. Names allow up to 32 characters; the default pattern accepts letters, digits, underscores and hyphens. rename and relocate additionally require sparrow.command.edit_warp.rename and sparrow.command.edit_warp.relocate. Use /del-warp to delete a warp. With permission-restrict enabled, viewing and using a warp requires sparrow.warp.use.<lowercase-name>. Management still uses command permissions. Configure cooldowns, warmups and arrival effects under teleport-options; see Teleport options. Select a warp in /warp-list to check its world and coordinates before choosing the travel button.
# Example: require a separate permission for each warp permission-restrict: true

Cooldowns, warmups and arrival effects are configured in each feature's own file. For example, in features/home.yml: teleport-options: cooldown: 5m warmup: duration: 5s cancel_on_move: true cancel_on_damage: true display: action_bar invulnerability: 5s after_sound: entity.enderman.teleport overrides: - permission: sparrow.home.teleport.staff cooldown: 0s warmup: duration: 0s - permission: sparrow.home.teleport.vip cooldown: 1m warmup: duration: 3s Option Meaning cooldown Cross-server cooldown starting after a successful teleport; 0s disables it. warmup.duration Wait before departure; 0s teleports immediately. cancel_on_move / cancel_on_damage Cancel the countdown after moving over half a block, changing worlds or taking damage. display action_bar, title, boss_bar, chat or none. invulnerability Protection duration after arrival. after_sound Arrival sound; an empty string or zero volume disables it. overrides Select the first matching traveler permission. Omitted options inherit; a supplied warmup replaces the entire option. Warmups also accept boss_bar_color, boss_bar_overlay, warmup_sound and cancel_sound. Sounds accept a name or name,volume,pitch, such as entity.enderman.teleport,0.5,1.

Feature Configuration location Home, Warp, TPA, RTP teleport-options in their respective features/<feature>.yml. Back, DeathBack back.teleport-options and deathback.teleport-options in features/back.yaml. Spawn teleport-options in features/spawn.yml; supports only cooldowns, warmups and permission overrides. Spawn uses hyphenated warmup fields, such as cancel-on-move and boss-bar-color, and defaults to a 0s warmup. The other features above default to a 5m cooldown, 5s warmup and 5s arrival protection. Cooldowns are separate per feature, including separate Back and DeathBack cooldowns. See Landing rules for destination selection.

Each feature defines how it chooses a landing position. Feature Destination selection Spawn, Home, Warp, offline teleport Saved or configured coordinates. TPA, patrol The target player's position. Back, DeathBack Check the original coordinates, then search within 4 blocks horizontally and 8 blocks up or down. RTP Search randomly within the configured region; surface scanning in ordinary worlds, cavity scanning in ceiling dimensions such as the Nether. World Check the destination, then search within 8 blocks horizontally and 16 blocks up or down if needed. Safety searches check boundaries, collisions, support and hazardous blocks. Back, DeathBack and RTP reject water, leaf support and Nether-roof locations by default. World allows shallow water with the head above the surface. For Back, DeathBack and World, --unsafe allows the original coordinates if the search fails. RTP ends without teleporting when it cannot find a safe location. There is no general YAML processor list for changing these rules. Developers can combine search rules and processors through the Teleport API.
